message.content: The sea can take on a range of colors depending on depth, weather, and the light conditions. In clear, shallow waters it often looks turquoise or greenish‑blue, while deeper ocean water tends to appear a deep, rich blue. On calm days with a clear sky, the sea can even reflect a bright, almost white hue. So, the “color” of the sea is not fixed—it shifts from green to blue to turquoise, and sometimes even gray or black in stormy or murky conditions.
